title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
statement: Two warehouse scanners each produce a sorted (ascending) list of integer package weights, a and b. Either list may be empty, but together they contain at least one weight. Return the median weight of the combined collection as a float: conceptually merge both lists into one sorted sequence; if its length is odd the median is the middle element (as a float, e.g. 9.0), and if even it is the average of the two middle elements (e.g. 4.5). Duplicates count once per occurrence. Your solution must run in O(log(min(m, n))) time, where m and n are the list lengths -- fully merging the lists is not acceptable. Hint at the required shape: binary search the partition index in the SHORTER list and derive the other list's cut so the left halves together hold (m + n + 1) // 2 elements, using -infinity/+infinity sentinels at the edges.
hints: A full merge is O(m + n). What could you binary search over so that each guess discards half the possibilities? Think about where you'd cut one list, not where a value lives.

Cut the SHORTER list at index i and force j = (m + n + 1) // 2 - i in the longer one, so the two left halves always hold half the elements. The cut is valid exactly when a[i-1] <= b[j] and b[j-1] <= a[i]; treat out-of-range edges as -infinity / +infinity sentinels.

Binary search i in [0, m] on the shorter list: if a[i-1] > b[j] move hi = i - 1, if b[j-1] > a[i] move lo = i + 1. On a valid cut, odd total -> float(max(left maxima)); even total -> (max(left maxima) + min(right minima)) / 2.0.
